definition: A testing environment specifically designed to evaluate an AI system's susceptibility to prompt injection attacks before deployment.
details: Prompt injection sandboxes allow developers to systematically probe agentic systems for vulnerabilities to malicious instructions embedded in tool outputs or processed content, as part of a broader security testing process.

explainer.lead: A prompt injection sandbox is a testing environment for evaluating an AI system's susceptibility to prompt injection before deployment. It matters because agentic systems can be probed for vulnerabilities systematically ahead of release.

tiers.eli5: It is like a crash-test track for cars: you slam the system with nasty inputs in a safe place before it meets real users.
tiers.practitioner: Developers use sandboxes to probe agentic systems for vulnerabilities to malicious instructions embedded in tool outputs or processed content, as part of broader security testing. A pitfall is that pre-deployment findings may not cover every production input.
tiers.paperLevel: A dedicated environment where AI systems are tested for susceptibility to prompt injection before deployment; it is one component of a broader security testing process.

explainer.example: Before launch, an agent is fed tool outputs containing hidden malicious instructions to see whether it follows them.
